tool: ## Video: A Brief History of Neural Networks
- id: vHISTORY010
- thumbnail_url: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/vHISTORY010/hqdefault.jpg
- published_at: 2024-01-15 10:00:00+00:00
  - [start=67 end=105 relevance=76.4] In 1969 Minsky and Papert proved a single perceptron cannot solve the XOR problem. Funding dried up, and the field entered what we now call the first AI winter.
  - [start=141 end=174 relevance=68.9] Expert systems overpromised in the late 80s and a second AI winter followed. Neural nets survived in a few stubborn labs in Canada.
  - [start=105 end=141 relevance=56.3] The thaw came in 1986, when Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams popularized backpropagation, showing multi-layer networks could learn internal representations.
  - [start=32 end=67 relevance=55.1] It starts in 1958 with Frank Rosenblatt's perceptron, a single artificial neuron that learned to classify simple images by adjusting its weights.
  - [start=0 end=32 relevance=55.0] Welcome to NeuralBytes. Today we trace the history of neural networks, from a room-sized machine in the 1950s to the models writing poetry today.
## Video: GANs: How Machines Learn to Create
- id: vGAN0000005
- thumbnail_url: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/vGAN0000005/hqdefault.jpg
- published_at: 2024-09-30 10:00:00+00:00
  - [start=0 end=30 relevance=59.8] Generative adversarial networks taught machines to create images that never existed. Here's how the trick works.
  - [start=68 end=102 relevance=56.7] Think of a counterfeiter and a detective: the counterfeiter improves until the detective can no longer tell the difference. That equilibrium is the training goal.
  - [start=30 end=68 relevance=55.0] A GAN is two networks locked in a game: a generator that fabricates samples from random noise, and a discriminator that tries to tell fakes from real data.
## Video: Fine-Tuning LLMs on a Budget
- id: vFINETUNE07
- thumbnail_url: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/vFINETUNE07/hqdefault.jpg
- published_at: 2025-03-15 10:00:00+00:00
  - [start=66 end=107 relevance=56.0] LoRA - low-rank adaptation - freezes the base model and trains only tiny low-rank adapter matrices inserted into each layer. You typically touch well under one percent of the parameters and can merge the adapter back in afterwards.
  - [start=107 end=144 relevance=55.3] QLoRA goes further: quantize the frozen base model to four bits, then train LoRA adapters on top. A single consumer GPU can fine-tune a model that would otherwise need a cluster.
  - [start=179 end=215 relevance=55.1] Always hold out an evaluation set and watch it during training - on small datasets an LLM can memorize the training examples in a couple of epochs, and the eval curve is how you catch it.
## Video: AI Ethics: Bias in Machine Learning
- id: vETHICS0009
- thumbnail_url: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/vETHICS0009/hqdefault.jpg
- published_at: 2025-01-20 10:00:00+00:00
  - [start=177 end=213 relevance=59.1] Regulation is arriving - the EU AI Act classifies systems by risk and puts hard obligations on high-risk uses like hiring and credit scoring.
